rationale: Implemented the discriminator the last interpretation named, and the draft-side run answers it: the three rejections are not re-applied entries. The new operands report applied_before and applying_before for the node at the moment the batch is consumed, plus reapplied_entry = (entry index <= applied_before). For the rejections at seed 35 the results are: node 3 step 22 applied_before=3 applying_before=3 entry_index=4 reapplied_entry=false; node 1 step 23 identical; node 4 step 31 applied_before=0 applying_before=0 entry_index=4 reapplied_entry=false (a freshly rebuilt node consuming its log from the start). In every case the batch's entry index is applied_before+1 or the node's first entry, so the harness applied committed entries in log order and did not re-present an already-applied entry - which refutes the double-application/off-by-one reading that the previous operands could not exclude, and leaves the target-side reading standing: a node consuming its own committed log in order is handed a joint-entering change at index 4 term 2 while its tracker is joint. What is still unprinted, and what the next receipt should carry, is the type/term of the entries before index 4 at the rejecting node, because that determines how the node's tracker became joint without a preceding leave entry - i.e. whether the proposal that put a second joint-entering change in the log was one the leader's alreadyPending/alreadyJoint rewrite should have turned into a normal entry. I therefore request fresh execution of these bytes rather than extending the draft-side claim further.

scope.description: Thirteenth revision of the same fixed harness; probes A-C and the deterministic joint-change case are unchanged. The sweep keeps the configuration targets, application lag, joint transitions, restarts, liveness witness and recovered apply guard, and the first three rejections now emit invalid_change_apply with the node's applied_before and applying_before pointers at the start of the apply batch, the entry's index, term, change count and joint flag, the node's applied/committed after the attempt, joint_now, and reapplied_entry (entry index <= applied_before). invariant_sweep_summary still reports all counters including invalid_change_applies and invalid_change_reasons.
assumptions: Everything comes from the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, newNetwork, nextEnts, confChangeToMsg, applyConfChange, hasUnappliedConfChanges, promotable, newRaft, SetHardState); no production logic is modified.

reapplied_entry is computed as entry index <= applied_before, which is the harness-level test for 'this entry was already applied'; it cannot detect a re-application that happens with applied_before already advanced past the whole batch.
The operands still do not print the entries before the rejected index, which is the next thing needed to see how the tracker became joint.
Randomness is fixed per seed; counts are descriptive, not rates.

experiment.prefix: For each of 60 seeds: build nodes 1..4 with newTestRaft(id,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); nt := newNetwork(nodes[1],nodes[2],nodes[3]) then nt.peers[4] = nodes[4]. For 60 steps pick one of MsgHup, MsgProp, tick(), isolate, recover, TransferLeader, a ConfChangeV2 proposal on the leader (single change, target drawn from node 4 or a non-leader member, half the time JointImplicit), a restart of a random node, or persist/apply of all nodes; after each step persist/apply nodes 1..4 (skipping one node about one time in six; capturing applied_before/applying_before per node; applying committed conf changes under recover and, for the first three rejections, emitting invalid_change_apply with the full operand set including reapplied_entry), then evaluate the four invariants and the liveness witness, finally emitting invariant_sweep_summary.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and sweep case as the previous execution, with the double-application discriminator added: applied_before, applying_before and reapplied_entry are now reported for each rejection. A draft-side run reported reapplied_entry=false for all three rejections with applied_before equal to entry_index-1 for nodes 3 and 1 and applied_before=0 for the rebuilt node 4, which is construction feedback only and is why isolated execution is requested.
